title: Customer-tiered batch/cache advisor with safe-apply guardrails
text:
Customer-tiered batch/cache advisor with safe-apply guardrails

description:
Goal: build an automated advisor and safe-apply system that generates and enforces per-customer and per-route batching+cache recommendations. The system should: (1) derive segmentation (customer tiers, route classes, allowlists/denylists) from traffic patterns and config rules, (2) produce conservative recommended config changes (batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, caching scopes, segmentation overrides) with an explainable rationale, and (3) apply those changes using a staged, observable, and rollback-capable orchestration path so customer-facing SLAs are preserved.

acceptance_criteria:
Advisor produces recommendations for at least 80% of high-volume routes across 3 pilot customers
Each recommendation includes expected cost delta, expected latency impact (p50/p95), uncertainty score, and rule provenance
Safe-apply orchestration allows canary rollouts with automated metric checks and automatic rollback on threshold breaches
Console UI shows per-customer diffs, an approval flow, and audit log entries for every apply/rollback
We validate advisor recommendations in shadow mode for two weeks without customer-visible apply and report no >0.5% increase in error-rate across test routes
Integration tests for allowlist/denylist enforcement and tier-based overrides with at least 95% pass rate in CI

implementation_notes:
Segmentation model: combine static attributes (customer tier, SLA level) with dynamic signal (median sequence length, request rate, cold-start frequency) to assign {route,customer} to an optimization profile
Recommendation engine: rules + heuristic scorer that outputs candidate config changes with delta estimates. Start with deterministic heuristics (safe defaults) and add a small ML ranking model in a follow-up spike
Safe-apply orchestration: create a controller that supports dry-run, shadow-apply, canary % steps (0, 5, 25, 100) and monitors latency p50/p95, tail latency, token throughput, 5xx rate and model output quality via prompt-based checks
Rollback policy: immediate rollback on >10% p95 latency regression or >2x error-rate vs baseline for canary step; automatic rollback window configurable per-customer
Operator tooling: add a console diff view showing token-cost estimate, expected monthly savings, and a link to the simulator that replays sampled requests under candidate config
Auditability: every apply must write an immutable entry to audit-log service with before/after configs, owner, and reason. Integrate with existing RBAC and SSO flows
Implementation path: build recommendation-only pipeline -> run in shadow mode -> enable safe-apply with manual approval -> enable automatic scheduled applies for Tier C (low-risk) customers
Metric instrumentation: per-route cost-per-token, tokens/s, batching rate, cache hit ratio, kv-cache hit latency; expose to console and alerts (PagerDuty only on P0 regressions)
Testing plan: create synthetic replay jobs to validate behavior for cold-start heavy customers and long-seq customers to ensure no regression in 95th percentile latency
Data retention & privacy: recommendations may reference aggregated usage stats. Do not surface raw customer request content in the UI. Follow privacy guidance in privacy-team/confluence

comments:
2025-02-13 - Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/ENG-31765). Agreed pilot customers: AcmeRetail, NimbusAnalytics, and SolaceAI.
2025-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Completed spike comparing heuristic vs simulation cost estimates. Heuristics are conservative (avg 12% savings vs sim 16%). PR with simulator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4027
2025-02-24 - Product: Suggested adding explicit allowlist for routes that cannot be batched due to streaming requirements. Marked as blocker for initial auto-apply for those routes.
2025-02-28 - Design: Provided mockups for Console diff and approval flow (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/mockups-ENG-31765). Requesting smaller text for change rationale box.
2025-03-02 - Security: Quick review requested. We need to confirm audit-log retention and that no customer payloads are stored. Security checklist created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/opt-advisor-checklist
2025-03-03 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype controller accepted in architecture review. Next: instrument 3 pilot routes for shadow-run and add auto-metric checks. Created work items for integration tests.
